title: Emrys and the Inventory
premise: Bram Eastwick, a man who writes other people's words for a living while sending unsent postcards to his burned-down childhood home, learns that the house on Marrow Lane is being auctioned by the city. Returning to bid, he collides with Odile, the foster sister he abandoned twenty years ago, who now works for the auction house and holds the only surviving inventory of everything they lost. As Bram and Odile itemize their past object by object, they uncover that the fire was no accident and that the man responsible now sits on the city council deciding the neighborhood's fate. In the end, Bram publicly reads aloud the letter he has written for two decades, forcing the truth into the record, losing the house but winning back Odile and, finally, his own voice.
about_author: Xanthe Villalobos is a former estate appraiser who spent years cataloguing the belongings of strangers before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted bus depot in coastal Oregon, where she still answers every letter she receives by hand.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet him in his meticulous, walled-off life: ghostwriting apologies and love letters for clients, mailing postcards to an address that no longer exists. A legal notice about the Marrow Lane auction cracks his routine open. The emotional beat is dread disguised as indifference—the first tremor of a man discovering invisibility was a choice someone else made for him.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Odile at the auction house. She recognizes Bram's name on the bidder list and confronts him among the boxed remnants of their childhood. Their hostile reconciliation unfolds through objects: a dented lunchbox, a melted hairbrush, her mother's ring listed as 'unclaimed.' The beat is grief sharpening into anger as Odile reveals she knows the fire's true cause—and who profited.

chapters.title: Everything Must Go
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, rising tension. He investigates Councilman Reeve Voss, the slumlord turned civic benefactor whose insurance claim matches the fire too neatly, while Odile risks her job to pull the original inventory ledger. When Voss offers Bram hush money dressed as a settlement, Bram almost takes it—until he finds his own childhood letter in the evidence box, never delivered. Beat: temptation, then resolve.

chapters.title: Out Loud, Before the Last Bus
chapters.summary: Shared POV at the auction itself. Instead of bidding, Bram takes the podium and reads the twenty-year-old letter aloud—naming the fire, the dead neighbor, Voss—while Odile distributes copies of the ledger to the crowd. The house sells to a community land trust; justice arrives outside any courtroom. Final beat: Bram and Odile ride the rerouted last bus together, saying goodbye properly at last, out loud.
